items.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025
items.q: And the supporting cast was ridiculous, I mean McCoy and Jimmy Garrison and Elvin.

ctx.x: Yeah. I started listening, you know I listened a lot to that radio station and of course Coltrane, as many other people were, I was fixated on Coltrane. I mean it was like a religion for me. And for many others as well. It doesn’t matter like what country you’re from, if you’re white or black or Muslim, Christian, Jewish, it doesn’t matter. He had a transcendent message that he was broadcasting through his music that affected many people in this deeply spiritual and religious way. I mean I compare him to Bach. I…

do. Because he was so mathematical at the same time as he was so spiritual. And the supporting cast was ridiculous, I mean McCoy and Jimmy Garrison and Elvin. I mean this is something that doesn’t happen too often in the history of music where you get four individuals with such amazing individual contributions and that are all playing together as one mind. And so this was overwhelming for me. But then I did of course get into all sorts of other people. I remember the Sonny Rollins “Live at the Village Vanguard”…

You just made me think of something I heard you say in a – I don't know if it was in an interview but, so I’m going to quote you. It says, “People may think – it looks like we’re in a trance when we’re playing, ‘cause we are.”
